title: Station Meridian Rising
premise: Silas Nakamura, navigator of the aging freighter Meridian Rising, has spent eleven years hauling cargo along a route between colonies that cut ties after a war nobody will name. The ship's hold holds something worse than cargo: memory backups of the colonists who died when the relay network fell, including a copy of Silas's own sister, waiting for a signal that never came. When children on both colonies begin sharing an identical dream — a beacon singing from dead space — Silas realizes the relay at the edge of the silence is still transmitting, and someone is using it to reach the sleeping minds. Racing a rival salvage crew and the failing backup cores, Silas must choose between waking the dead and protecting the living, ending with Silas broadcasting the truth of the war to both colonies and finally letting the backups — including his sister's — choose for themselves whether to wake.
about_author: Hazel Iversen is a former radio astronomer who traded observatory shifts for the writing desk, drawn to stories about the signals we send and the silences we keep. She lives on the coast, where she claims the fog is the best editor she's ever had.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A routine run between colonies Verity and Halcyon establishes the fractured worlds, the ship's creaking systems, and the sealed hold Silas refuses to enter. His co-pilot, Wren Osei, presses him about what's really down there. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Children of the Static
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Docking at Halcyon, they find a classroom of children drawing the same impossible structure — a relay tower wreathed in aurora — and humming a melody no one taught them. One girl, Ama, grabs Wren's sleeve and calls her by a dead colonist's name. Emotional beat: unease blooming into dread.

chapters.title: What Sleeps in the Hold
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, with a flashback. Silas finally opens the hold and confronts the memory cores: forty-one colonists lost when the Meridian relay fell during the war, including his sister Noor's backup. The cores are warm — drawing power from somewhere, responding to something. Emotional beat: guilt cracking open.

chapters.title: The Same Dream
chapters.summary: Alternating Silas and Wren. The dream spreads to adults, then to Wren herself: a voice repeating coordinates in dead space, past the relay, where no one should be alive. The colonies blame each other, and port authorities threaten to seize the Meridian as the only ship rated for the route. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Departure Without Clearance
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They steal their own ship out of Halcyon's gravity well, pursued by a salvage crew called the Vantablack, whose captain, Ilsa Reyen, wants the cores' black-market value — and knows more about the war than she admits. Emotional beat: loyalty tested at the first hard turn.

chapters.title: The Silence Between
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In dead space, the ship's instruments fail and only the dream's coordinates hold true. Ama's voice comes through the comm — from a colony light-years behind them — reciting the same numbers. The cores in the hold begin to sing in their sleep. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by terror.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Version of the Truth
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, after the Vantablack forces a boarding standoff. Ilsa reveals the relay didn't fail — it was shut down deliberately to bury a colony's transmission of war crimes, and the children's dream is the buried signal finally breaking through. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning your grief was engineered.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They reach the relay and find its caretaker: a half-awake backup of the engineer who shut it down, keeping the signal suppressed out of a loyalty to the dead that curdled into a prison. He offers Silas the choice — restore the signal and expose everything, or let the sleepers rest in a merciful lie. Emotional beat: the book's moral hinge.

chapters.title: Signal Fire
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. The Vantablack arrives; Ilsa wants the relay destroyed to keep her own colony's complicity buried. Silas and Wren fight to hold the transmission tower while Noor's backup, briefly awake inside the relay's systems, helps them route the signal past the jamming. The truth broadcasts to both colonies. Emotional beat: sacrifice and reckoning at full burn.

chapters.title: Waking
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, resolution. Weeks later, the colonies reopen contact, raw and unfinished. The backups, given the choice, mostly choose to rest — but a few wake, Noor among them, and Silas meets his sister as a stranger who knows all his stories. Ama and the children's dream fades into an ordinary lullaby. Emotional beat: grief resolved not by erasure but by truth, and belonging rebuilt on honest ground.
